text: Ten fictional nonprofit programme passages, each with eight quote variants for citation-checker testing.

passages.source_passage: The Saltmarsh Coast Early Warning Initiative, run by Harbourlight Resilience Trust in the Venmora district, reached its mid-point in March 2023. Evaluators found that 41 village alert committees had been formed against a target of fifty. Siren towers were installed in twelve fishing settlements, and drill participation rose to 68 percent of registered households. However, the text-message alert system was not tested during the cyclone season because the network contract had lapsed. Committee members reported that older residents rarely trusted sirens alone and preferred door-to-door warnings from volunteers. The evaluation team did not find evidence that evacuation routes had been mapped in the three inland hamlets. It recommends that the remaining budget prioritise route mapping and a renewed telecom agreement before the next monsoon.

variants.added_negation: Siren towers were not installed in twelve fishing settlements, and drill participation rose to 68 percent of registered households.
variants.removed_negation: However, the text-message alert system was tested during the cyclone season because the network contract had lapsed.

variants.paraphrase: The evaluators saw no proof that escape routes had been charted in the three hamlets away from the coast.

passages.source_passage: During the 2022–23 programme year, the Lanterns Evening Literacy Network operated 34 classes across the Orvale and Kestrin valleys with support from the Brightwater Foundation. A total of 812 adults enrolled, and 63% of them completed the full nine-month cycle. Most learners were women working in market trading or domestic service. Facilitators noted that attendance dropped sharply during the harvest weeks, when many learners could not leave the fields before dark. We did not open the four new classes planned for Kestrin town because no suitable venues with electric lighting were available. Learners who completed the cycle read, on average, two levels higher than at intake. Next year we will pilot solar lamps so that classes can meet in homes rather than halls.

passages.source_passage: Quarterly monitoring for the Greenfurrow Farmer Field School Network covered 26 schools in the Amberleigh and Tolva sub-counties between April and June 2024. Field officers recorded that 540 smallholders attended at least eight of the twelve scheduled sessions. Adoption of mulching on demonstration plots reached 72 percent, up from 45 percent at baseline. Seed of the drought-tolerant sorghum variety did not arrive until late May, so most groups were not able to plant comparison plots this season. No school reported pest outbreaks serious enough to require spraying. Women made up just over half of active members, but they held only three of the 26 facilitator posts. The team recommends that the next cohort of facilitators be recruited from experienced female members.

passages.source_passage: At its mid-term point in September 2023, the Safe Harbour Case Management Service in Kelvari camp had registered 1,930 protection cases, roughly 40 percent of them involving unaccompanied or separated children. Caseworkers from the Meridian Refugee Council conducted follow-up visits within seven days for most high-risk cases. The evaluation did not find a functioning referral pathway to legal aid, and several families said they were never told how to appeal registration decisions. Staff turnover was high, with eleven of the original 24 caseworkers leaving in the first year. Interviewed children described the drop-in space as safe and welcoming. The evaluators recommend a dedicated legal officer and a shorter, translated information leaflet for new arrivals.

passages.source_passage: Dornak district, in the eastern uplands of Pellamar, has a population of about 58,000 people, most of whom live in scattered hamlets more than two kilometres from a protected water source. A 2021 survey by the Clearspring Water Alliance found that only 31% of households had access to an improved latrine. Many hand-dug wells dry up between January and April, forcing women and girls to walk to the Ruvu river. Diarrhoeal disease remains the second most common reason for clinic visits among children under five. Previous borehole projects in the district were not accompanied by community maintenance committees, and eight of the fourteen boreholes drilled since 2015 are no longer functional. This proposal seeks to combine new boreholes with trained committees and household latrine promotion.

passages.source_passage: Before each distribution day, volunteers must check that every household on the register has been visited during the census week. Each household receives one net for every two sleeping spaces, up to a maximum of four nets. Do not hand nets to children under 15 unless an adult household member is present to sign. Remind families that nets should be aired in the shade for 24 hours before first use. Never cut the packaging open in front of the queue, as this has caused crowding in past campaigns. In the 2022 Marrowfield campaign, volunteers who demonstrated hanging a net saw usage rates about 20 percent higher at follow-up. Report any shortfall in stock to your Tallis Health Partnership supervisor the same afternoon.

passages.source_passage: In the 2023 school year, the Puente Abierto Scholarship Programme supported 215 girls attending secondary schools in the highland municipalities of San Rafael del Monte and Las Cuevitas. Each scholarship covered fees, uniforms, and a monthly transport stipend of 300 quetzales. Retention was strong: 94 percent of scholars finished the year, compared with roughly 70 percent of girls in the same grades district-wide. Nine students left the programme, most often because of family migration rather than marriage or pregnancy. We were not able to hire the second mentor planned for Las Cuevitas, so mentoring sessions there took place monthly instead of fortnightly. No scholar was asked to repay support after leaving. In 2024 we hope to add 40 new places, subject to continued funding from the Alder Grove Trust.

passages.source_passage: This update covers the Willowmere Community Counselling Service from July to December 2024. Our eight lay counsellors held 1,146 individual sessions and ran 22 peer support groups across the Brackenford estates. Waiting times for a first appointment fell from six weeks to under three. Clients completing at least five sessions showed an average 38 percent reduction in distress scores on the standard screening tool. We have not yet secured a clinical supervisor for the evening shift, and the board should note that counsellors there currently work without on-site backup. Referrals from the two local GP practices have doubled, but no referrals have come from the secondary school despite outreach in October. Management requests board approval to advertise a part-time supervisor post in January.

passages.source_passage: The mid-term evaluation of the Ironbridge Youth Skills Centre in Tamsford examined the first two intakes, totalling 312 trainees aged 17 to 24. Completion rates were 81 percent in welding, tailoring and solar installation courses combined. Six months after graduation, 46 percent of completers were in paid work or running their own business. Employers praised trainees' practical skills but said many graduates were not confident in job interviews. The planned apprenticeship placements with the Tamsford Port Authority did not materialise in 2023, which limited workplace exposure. Young women were concentrated in tailoring, where earnings were lowest, and none enrolled in solar installation. The evaluators recommend a structured employability module and targeted outreach to encourage women into higher-paying trades.

passages.source_passage: Primary schools in the Koraba prefecture of northern Sanvela serve some of the poorest communities in the region. A 2022 assessment by the Tamarind Child Nutrition Fund found that 37 percent of pupils in Grade 3 were underweight and that nearly one in four arrived at school without having eaten breakfast. Attendance falls by as much as a third during the lean season from June to August. None of the 48 public primary schools in the prefecture currently provides a daily meal, and the government feeding scheme hasn't reached Koraba since 2019. Local farmers' cooperatives already grow millet, cowpeas and groundnuts that could supply school kitchens. This proposal requests funding to provide a hot midday meal to 9,600 pupils over three school years.
